title: A bike-delivery bakery
transcript:
A: Today I'm with Lena Ortiz, who started a bread delivery business two years ago. Lena, how did it start?
B: Honestly, by accident. I was baking bread at home for friends, and one of them said, "Why don't you sell it?" But I didn't have a shop, and I couldn't afford one. So I borrowed my cousin's bike, the one with a big basket, and I delivered the bread myself, before breakfast.
A: And people liked it?
B: They loved it. Within three months I had about sixty regular customers. It was exhausting, though. I was getting up at three in the morning.
A: So have you opened a shop now?
B: Not yet. I'm thinking about it, but a shop means rent, and I'm not sure I want that kind of stress. At the moment I've hired two students to do the deliveries, and that works well. Maybe next year I'll decide.

title: Running club welcome
transcript: Welcome, everyone, to the Saturday Running Club. I'm Gary, one of the leaders. Before we start, a few things. Firstly, this isn't a race. Most of you are beginners, so we'll run for two minutes, then walk for one minute, and repeat that for half an hour. If you can't talk while you're running, you're going too fast, so slow down. Secondly, wear good shoes. They don't have to be expensive, but old shoes can give you sore knees. Finally, we meet at the park gate at eight, but because it's getting cold, from next month we'll start at nine instead. There's tea in the hut afterwards, and it's free for members. Right, shall we go?
